office.name: Office of the County Executive, Manitowoc County
office.place: Manitowoc County, Wisconsin (county seat Manitowoc; cities of Manitowoc, Two Rivers and Kiel, plus towns and villages)
office.location: County Executive's office, Manitowoc County Courthouse, 1010 S. 8th St., Manitowoc, WI 54220 (county general line (920) 683-4000)
office.remit: Wisconsin county executive in a county under 750,000 (Wis. Stat. 59.17): the county's chief executive and administrative officer. Appoints and supervises most department heads (subject to County Board confirmation), appoints members of most boards and commissions, submits the annual budget to the 25-member County Board of Supervisors, may veto resolutions and ordinances, and signs contracts and conveyances for the county. Departments under the executive include Human Services, Public Health, Highway, Public Works (buildings, Expo grounds and Ice Center, recycling center, tax-deeded property, purchasing), Planning, Parks and Land Information, Emergency Services (Emergency Management and the Joint Dispatch Center for 911), Finance, Corporation Counsel and the ADRC. The County Board sets the levy and adopts the budget; standing committees (Finance, Highway, Public Works, Public Safety, Personnel) and boards (Human Services Board, Board of Health, Planning and Park Commission, Expo-Ice Center Board) oversee departments. The executive's own office is small: the executive, an executive assistant and an administrative and communications coordinator, all county employees paid from the county budget.

succession.rule: Wis. Stat. 59.17(7): 'A vacancy in the office of county executive shall be filled temporarily, within 30 days of the date of the vacancy, by appointment by the chairperson of the board, subject to confirmation by the board, from among electors of the county. Within 7 days following the occurrence of the vacancy, the clerk shall order a special election to be held under s. 8.50 to fill the vacancy.' Wis. Stat. 59.17(8)(b): the board chair immediately succeeds to the office until the board has confirmed an appointment. Wis. Stat. 8.50(2)(a): the special election is held not less than 62 nor more than 77 days from the date of the order (with exceptions for elections held with the spring or general election); a primary, if needed, is 4 weeks before (8.50(2)(b)).
succession.timeline: Tue Sept 1, 2026: the previous county executive's resignation takes effect (no reason given in the drive); County Board Chair Ron Zastrow (fictional) becomes acting county executive under 59.17(8)(b). Thu Sept 3: the County Clerk orders a special election for Tue Nov 17, 2026 (75 days after the order). Tue Sept 8: Zastrow announces his appointment of Joel Stahlberg. Tue Sept 15: County Board confirms, 21-3 (one excused). Wed Sept 16: oath of office, Courthouse. Stahlberg filed nomination papers for the special election; two candidates qualified, so no special primary is held. The winner serves the rest of the four-year term that began in April 2026 (to April 2030).
succession.election_timing_note: The seat is on the ballot four weeks after the scenario clock (Nov 17 special election). The Nov 3 general election is a separate ballot. The 8.50(2) window (62-77 days) rules out holding the special election with Nov 3 (the concurrent-with-general-election order window had closed) and with the April 2027 spring election (too far out for a September order).
succession.real_context: The real Manitowoc County executive elected in April 2026 is still in office; the resignation, the appointment and the special election are fictional. The real executive and board are never named.
sources: https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/document/statutes/8.50 (special elections: 8.50(2)(a) 62-77 days from the order; primary 4 weeks before; checked 2026-10-07)
https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/statutes/statutes/17.pdf (17.21 covers sheriff, clerk, treasurer, supervisors etc.; county executive vacancies are under 59.17(7))
